summary: This focused review covers 17 units, 10 date items and 5 people. All five attestation claims are defects. Each puts a figure named in a later allusion, kinship reference or dream (Lü Meng, Wu Chen, Xia Ji, Chao’s unnamed father and De’s father) on dates the cited units do not state, mostly outside life or reign windows. The five hints depend on those claims. For Wu Chen and Xia Ji, BC 584 also does not fit the BC 598 event alluded to. Each claim should be replaced by an undated retrospective reference and each hint withdrawn. Identities, people and the uncertainty about the unnamed father are left as they are. This is not a whole-chapter audit.

itemChecks.event: Murong Chui tells Murong De he is no longer 吳下阿蒙, a retrospective allusion made in the Former Yan period.
itemChecks.reason: s0011 is Chui quoting a proverb about Lü Meng. It does not record any act Lü Meng performed and gives no date for him. The stored AD 200–219 interval comes from an outside life window, not from this unit. The allusion was made more than a century later, so attesting Lü Meng as active in that interval from s0011 confuses the time of the allusion with the time of the person.

itemChecks.event: Murong De recalls that King Zhuang of Chu accepted Wu Chen’s remonstrance when he destroyed Chen.
itemChecks.reason: s0016 is De’s retrospective example. It gives no date and records no act by Wu Chen in De’s time. The stored year BC 584 also does not fit the event recalled. King Zhuang’s destruction of Chen and Wu Chen’s remonstrance about Xia Ji belong to BC 598 (Zuozhuan, Duke Xuan 11). BC 584 is the year Wu Chen went to Wu. The chapter gives none of these dates, so the attestation should not be kept.

evidence.quote: 昔楚莊滅陳，納巫臣之諫而棄夏姬

itemChecks.event: Murong De recalls that King Zhuang of Chu set Xia Ji aside after Wu Chen’s remonstrance.
itemChecks.reason: s0016 mentions Xia Ji only as part of De’s historical example. The stored year BC 584 is not in the source. It is also not the year of the event alluded to, which came after Chen fell in BC 598. A later allusion cannot attest her as active in any particular year, so the date claim should not be kept.

itemChecks.event: Murong De had earlier fetched his elder brother’s son Chao from Chang’an, and Chao arrives around the end of De’s reign.
itemChecks.reason: s0272 refers to Chao’s father only through the kinship term 其兄子. The father does nothing in this unit, and nothing shows he was alive in AD 403–405. Chao’s arrival dates Chao and De, not the father. Neither endpoint of the interval is attested for the father, so the claim confuses the time of the narration with the father’s own activity.

evidence.quote: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至

itemChecks.event: Murong De dreams that his late father, called 先帝, tells him to make Chao crown prince.
itemChecks.reason: s0273 records a dream in De’s last year, the first year of Yixi (s0276), in which the father appears as a dream speaker. The stored interval AD 337–348 is an outside reign window and is not stated in s0273 or s0274. A dream appearance is not the father’s own living activity in that window or in AD 405. The claim joins a later dream reference to an outside date, so it should not be kept.

itemChecks.event: Lü Meng’s active-date hint rests only on the Chui allusion to 吳下阿蒙.
itemChecks.reason: The only local dated evidence for AD 200–219 is claim-78, which s0011 does not support. Once that claim is removed, the owned units hold no dated evidence for this hint. The hint should be withdrawn and any life dates left to separate, cited research.

itemChecks.event: Wu Chen’s active-date hint rests only on De’s historical example of King Zhuang’s acceptance of his remonstrance.
itemChecks.reason: The hint BC 584 comes only from claim-81, which the source does not support. That year also does not fit the recalled remonstrance, which belongs to BC 598. With no supported dated item left, the hint should be withdrawn, not guessed.

itemChecks.event: Xia Ji’s active-date hint rests only on De’s historical example that King Zhuang set Xia Ji aside.
itemChecks.reason: The hint BC 584 comes only from claim-82, which neither the source nor the event alluded to supports. The owned units give no dated activity for Xia Ji, so the hint should be withdrawn.

itemChecks.event: The active-date hint for Chao’s unnamed father rests on Chao’s arrival at De’s court.
itemChecks.reason: The hint AD 405 comes only from claim-384. It treats a kinship reference made at Chao’s arrival as the father’s own activity. The unit does not show that the father was alive then, so the hint should be withdrawn and the father kept as an unnamed person.

itemChecks.event: The active-date hint for De’s father, who speaks in De’s dream, rests on an outside reign window.
itemChecks.reason: The hint AD 337–348 comes only from claim-385. The owned units contain only the later dream and the title 先帝, neither of which dates the father’s activity. The hint should be withdrawn for separate cited research.

personChecks.reason: I keep the person record and the 阿蒙 and 吳下阿蒙 names, which the s0011 allusion attests. The date data is wrong: the only attestation, claim-78, and the hint AD 200–219 are not supported by the owned units. The allusion should be kept as a retrospective reference, without dates.

I keep the person record and the name Wu Chen. The date data is wrong: claim-81 and the hint BC 584 are not attested, and that year also does not fit the BC 598 remonstrance alluded to. The reference should be kept as a retrospective event, without dates.
I keep the person record, the name Xia Ji and the sex. The date data is wrong: claim-82 and the hint BC 584 are not attested. The reference should be kept as a retrospective event, without dates.

I keep this as an unnamed person: Chao’s father and De’s elder brother, inferred only from 兄子. Do not name or merge him. The date data is wrong: claim-384 and the hint AD 405 do not attest his own activity, and the source does not show he was alive at Chao’s arrival.

I keep the person record and the existing identity, De’s father, called 先帝, as recorded. I don’t change the identity. The date data is wrong: claim-385 and the hint AD 337–348 come from an outside reign window and are attached to a dream in AD 405, not to the father’s own activity.

findings.problem: The Lü Meng attestation and hint (AD 200–219) take dates for a person mentioned only in Chui’s later allusion 吳下阿蒙 from an outside life window. s0011 gives no date.
findings.action: Remove claim-78, record an undated retrospective-reference event for p009 on s0011, and clear the hint p009. Keep the name claims and the identity.

findings.problem: The Wu Chen and Xia Ji attestations and hints (BC 584) date people mentioned only in De’s historical example. The source gives no date, and BC 584 does not fit the BC 598 remonstrance recalled.
findings.action: Remove claim-81 and claim-82, record undated retrospective-reference events on s0016, and clear the hints p012 and p013. Do not substitute BC 598 as an attestation of these people.

findings.problem: The attestation and hint for Chao’s unnamed father (AD 403–405, AD 405) treat a kinship reference made at Chao’s arrival as the father’s own activity.
findings.action: Remove claim-384, record an undated reference event on s0272, and clear the hint p163. Keep p163 unnamed and keep his kinship to p154 and p162 as strongly inferred.

findings.problem: The attestation and hint for De’s father (AD 337–348) attach an outside reign window to his appearance in De’s dream in AD 405.
findings.action: Remove claim-385, record an undated dream-figure reference on s0273, and clear the hint p164. Keep the existing identity and the dream-speech attribution.
